questions.text: An image tokenizer and a speech tokenizer both emit local code7. How should those codes be represented in a shared vocabulary that uses disjoint modality ranges?

options.A: Use global ID7 for both and discard modality information.
options.B: Map both codes to the same text token because their local IDs match.
options.C: Apply different modality offsets so they receive distinct global IDs.
options.D: Delete both codes because local code numbers must never repeat.

questions.explanation: Local code indices may repeat across codebooks; modality-specific offsets map them to distinct global IDs and prevent vocabulary collisions.

questions.text: An image codebook has100 entries and starts at global ID200. Using a contiguous range with an exclusive end, where should the next modality range begin?
questions.explanation: The image codes occupy IDs200 through299. The exclusive end and next available ID are200+100=300.

questions.text: route_inputs maps kind in ("speech", "voice") to "SpeechTokenizer residual-VQ" and uses "UNKNOWN" for unrecognized kinds. What paths result for kinds ["voice", "video"]?
questions.explanation: Voice is an explicit alias for speech. Video has no matching branch in this toy router, so it receives UNKNOWN; the helper only labels paths.
